Reasoning  

1. Planet (a): 1 M⊕ and 1 R⊕ → ρ ≈ 5.5 g cm⁻³ (Earth’s density).

2. Planet (b): density is given directly as ≈ 5.5 g cm⁻³.

3. Planet (c): same composition as Earth, but 5 M⊕.  
   • For rocky planets the mass–radius relation is roughly R ∝ M^0.27 (valid to ≲10 M⊕).  
   • R_c ≈ 5^0.27 R⊕ ≈ 1.54 R⊕.  
   • Volume ∝ R³ ⇒ V_c/V⊕ ≈ 1.54³ ≈ 3.65.  
   • Density ratio ρ_c/ρ⊕ = (M_c/M⊕)/(V_c/V⊕) ≈ 5 / 3.65 ≈ 1.37.  
   • ρ_c ≈ 1.37 × 5.5 g cm⁻³ ≈ 7.5 g cm⁻³.

4. Planet (d): same composition, 0.5 M⊕.  
   • R_d ≈ 0.5^0.27 R⊕ ≈ 0.83 R⊕.  
   • V_d/V⊕ ≈ 0.83³ ≈ 0.57.  
   • ρ_d/ρ⊕ ≈ 0.5 / 0.57 ≈ 0.88.  
   • ρ_d ≈ 0.88 × 5.5 g cm⁻³ ≈ 4.8 g cm⁻³.

Comparison:  
ρ_c (~7.5) > ρ_a (=ρ_b ≈5.5) > ρ_d (~4.8).

Thus planet (c) is the densest, corresponding to option (A).

Answer: A
